newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish fin min says ERM seems key to EMU.
newsitem.headline: Finnish fin min says ERM seems key to EMU.

text.p: Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Wednesday it seemed likely that belonging to the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) was an unconditional criterion for joining the third stage of EMU.

"The fact that the currency has been stable is hardly enough, but the general opinion especially in central Europe is that ERM is a system which one must join," Niinisto told a breakfast briefing for business executives and reporters.
"It seems that belonging to ERM is unconditional," he said.
"It has become very probable that belonging to the Exchange Rate Mechanism will be an absolute criterion," he said.

He repeated that the issue of linking the markka to the ERM "will be decided this autumn", adding that the government had taken a slight risk in not joining ERM in time to have been in the system for the required two years.
Asked if the external value of the markka was currently "too strong" to peg it to ERM, Niinisto said:

"The purpose of the (ERM) system is to promote stability. Finland has a two-year history of (exchange rate) stability. If a decision about ERM is made this autumn, this autumn's (exchange rate) is not decisive, but the two-year history (is)."

The national parliament will rule on Finnish participation in the third phase of Economic and Monetary Union, Niinisto said, adding the ruling for or against EMU entry would be made by a simple majority vote.

Some EMU critics have said the decision on joining the single currency should be made in constitutional order requiring a two-thirds majority and to take force in time for EMU's scheduled kick-off in January 1999. They said it would need a five-sixths majority to be declared urgent.
The five parties in Finland's left-right-green coalition government control 142 seats in the 200-strong single-house legislature.
Niinisto repeated the government's view it was obliged to make sure Finland fulfilled all EMU entry criteria to give parliament a real choice on EMU entry.
Niinisto said it was "completely clear" Finland would fulfil the EMU criteria by spring 1998, when EMU leaders are due to decide which countries will join the first wave of the single currency area.
